title: TT-Bio benchmarks: biomolecular structure prediction, design and binding affinity on Tenstorrent hardware
subtitle: Eight structure-prediction models, two binder-design models and one binding-affinity model at 512 residues, measured on Tenstorrent Blackhole and on NVIDIA H200, B200 and A100.
notes: This file is the only place numbers are edited. index.html reads it and derives everything else.
Never write a derived value here. Server throughput, cost per hour and both throughput-per-dollar charts are computed in the page from s_per_fold, accelerators, price and power.

A row is published only when every processor column is measured. A model with a blank column waits in perf/page_rows_pending.json until its missing cells exist, because a half-measured row still draws a bar and reads as a claim. scripts/site_publish_guard.py enforces this, --strip holds a row and --restore publishes it.

One cell per model per platform. A Tenstorrent cell is tt-bio main in its default mode, with its --fast run kept beside it under `fast`; an NVIDIA cell is the Anthropic kit's exact mode where the kit has the model (ref "kit") and the authors' own release where it does not (ref "stock"), with the other runs kept as `fast` and `stock`. Every Tenstorrent cell states its accuracy from the release gate (perf/bmk/gate_parity.py). Numbers come from state/bmk/BOARD.md through perf/bmk/board_to_page.py. A cell with no measurement gets a status and a reason, never an estimate.

The A100 appears twice: as a card, and as the DGX A100 640GB, the eight-GPU box NVIDIA sold that card in. The $175,000 that box carries is an assumed street price, not a vendor list price, and it is labelled as one everywhere it is used.
A design model carrying 'hidden': true keeps every measured cell here and is drawn nowhere. Delete that one line to publish the row again.

Every Tenstorrent cell states the board it was measured on. It inherits `measured_on` from its platform and overrides it only if it ran somewhere else. The column is priced as a p150a; the board that produced the number is a separate fact and is stated as one.

The embed block is measured but not published. All six rows carry "hidden": true and the page has no code that reads it, so the guard counts them out of the title, the subtitle and the meta description. site/README.md records what was run. Restoring the section means dropping the flags, putting the chart and the t-embed table back, and moving EXPECT_ROWS.embed in render_check.js in the same commit.

scope.description: CDK2 (PDB 1HCL) tandem-duplicated to 512 residues, one protein chain, no ligands, a fixed 35-sequence MSA.
scope.protocol: Warm runs, one prediction at a time on one accelerator, the same input on every platform, each model at its shipped settings. Tenstorrent runs tt-bio main in its default mode.
scope.nvidia_code: The GPUs run Anthropic's open kit for these models in exact mode where it has the model, and the authors' own release where it does not.
scope.nvidia_impl: Exact mode keeps the upstream arithmetic: checked on every GPU, it matched the unpatched package bit for bit where determinism can be switched on, and within 0.6 Å elsewhere.
scope.timed_region: Tenstorrent times the whole call, featurisation and file writing included. Most kit cells time the model call alone, which favours the NVIDIA column; RoseTTAFold3 is timed whole on both sides.
scope.accuracy: Every release scores each model against its official reference implementation on Blackhole, run the way people use it: with an MSA wherever the model takes one. Per-target results, thresholds and reproduction commands are in the repository's docs/implementation-parity.md.

cost_model.amortisation_basis: Four years is our assumption for an accelerator's useful life, one year shorter than the server life Amazon reports in its 10-Q.
cost_model.utilisation: The machine predicts continuously, so every hour of ownership is an hour of throughput.
cost_model.formula: Purchase price: predictions per hour ÷ price. Total cost of ownership: predictions per hour ÷ cost per hour, where cost per hour = price ÷ (4 × 8766 h) + power kW × $/kWh. Both are indexed to the DGX H200 at 1.00x.

models.server_charts_note: RFdiffusion3 is not on the per-server or per-dollar charts. Those charts scale seconds per job by accelerator count, and this row's two sides do not have the same lever: a batch of eight is worth 2.12x on the H200, 2.50x on the B200 and 1.79x on the A100, measured at shipped defaults with the H200 at 79 % of its 700 W and 98 % utilisation, while the Blackhole AI Processor gains 1.04x at 3844 atoms and does not fit a batch of eight. At batch 1 the Galaxy reads 1.20x a DGX H200; at each side's best batch it reads 0.57x, so the batch decides the sign rather than the size. The seconds chart keeps the row, because one at a time is the right protocol for latency. BoltzGen stays on both charts: its batched path drifts 0.5-2.8 A per slot, which makes a batched design a different design, so batch 1 is the production configuration on the GPU as well as here.

affinity.cond: Seconds per binding-affinity prediction on one AI Processor, warm, at shipped defaults. Shorter is better.
affinity.note: Nesso-1 needs a ligand and returns scalars, not a structure, so it runs a 512-residue protein plus one ligand (532 tokens) instead of the fold input.
affinity.methods: One protein plus one ligand at shipped defaults, 5 recycling steps, one prediction at a time. Tenstorrent figures are warm medians of four with input preparation inside the timer. GPU figures time one call of upstream's predict loop, with the RDKit conformer and ESM-2 embedding computed beforehand.

embed.methods: Six encoders at the shipped defaults, --fast off, mean pooling, no masked-LM logits. bfloat16 on both sides. attn_implementation sdpa is requested on the NVIDIA side and the harness counts the calls rather than trusting the flag. The input is one 512-residue sequence from scripts/gpu_vs_tt/fixtures/prot512.seq (sha256 141f7d47...), copied to fill the batch; both sides assert that digest before timing. Tenstorrent figures are warm medians of n=7 on one Blackhole AI Processor under benchlock with the loadavg recorded; NVIDIA figures are warm medians of n=15 on rented single-GPU nodes with the cold rep discarded. Every cell carries its own accuracy check: on Tenstorrent an all-finite pooled digest with the batch rows asserted identical, on NVIDIA the cosine of the bf16 output against an fp32 recomputation of the same forward, 0.999956 to 0.999996 against a 0.999 bar.

models.name: SaProt 35M
models.note: At 16.6 seq/s this row is slower than SaProt 1.3B at 23.4 on the same card, which reads as a page bug and is not one. SaProt 35M has a head dim of 24 (hidden 480 over 20 heads), neither tile-aligned nor aligned with the fused on-device rotary kernel, so the port splits heads, applies RoPE on host in fp32 and pads 24 to 32 on host, once per layer. That costs 35.2 ms per layer against 4.5-4.7 ms per layer for the two larger sizes at hidden 1280, and it is also why this is the widest-spread Tenstorrent row here at 13.0 %. Documented in docs/saprot-parity.md under "35M host-side RoPE path"; a fix is proposed, not landed.

caveats: Compare a model with itself across hardware, not rows with each other: each model runs its own recycle and step counts.

The NVIDIA cells ran on 14 and 15 October 2026 on rented single-GPU nodes, A100 with AMD EPYC 7513 hosts, H200 with Intel Xeon Platinum 8568Y+ and B200 with Intel Xeon Platinum 8559C. Host speed is not corrected for.
Each kit pins its own torch and CUDA per model; every cell's hover text names its versions.
